issues.description: Method: PersonService.addParent(Person, Person). The problem statement and the template declare and document the method as addParent(Person person, Person parent) where the first parameter is the child (person) and the second is the parent. In the solution implementation the method signature uses the same parameter types but the parameter names are swapped (addParent(Person parent, Person person)). The parameter order by type remains (Person, Person) so code compiles and callers (e.g., PersonResource) are unaffected, but the swapped parameter names in the solution are inconsistent with the specification and the template and can confuse students about which argument represents the child vs. the parent.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the parameters in the solution implementation to match the problem statement and template: change the method declaration in the solution to 'public Person addParent(Person person, Person parent)' and update the implementation body to use 'person' for the child and 'parent' for the parent. This keeps behavior identical while removing the source of confusion for students.
